performance.title: Piece Counting and Dynamic Weighing Explained
performance.description: What LA204's two built-in apps take off a routine lab's plate.
body: Counting small components by hand is slow and error-prone past a handful of pieces, and weighing anything that shifts, settles, or breathes on the pan, powders, granules, or restless small samples, makes the reading drift before it stabilizes. LA204's two built-in apps are built around exactly those two everyday problems.

The piece counting app establishes an average unit weight from a reference sample, then converts any weighed batch into a piece count automatically. The dynamic weighing app takes repeated readings over a short window and calculates a stable average, so an unsettled sample still returns a trustworthy result instead of a fluctuating one.

performance.description: What FACT adjustment and leveling guidance actually remove from getting MR204 set up correctly.
body: An analytical balance that isn't level reads wrong before a single sample even touches the pan, and getting it level by eye, watching a bubble indicator and adjusting feet by feel, is easy to get slightly wrong without noticing. performance.title: Dual-Range Weighing Explained
performance.description: What SmartPan actually does when a sample crosses from micro-scale into everyday range.
body: A single-range analytical balance forces a choice: fine enough for micro-scale samples, or capable of everyday capacity, but rarely both without buying two instruments. That's a real problem for a pharma lab weighing a wide spread of sample sizes across a single day, from milligram-level actives to gram-level excipients.

MX205DU's SmartPan technology resolves that by running two ranges on one pan: 0.01 mg readability up to 82 g for micro-scale work, switching automatically to 0.1 mg readability up to 220 g once the sample calls for it. The switch happens without recalibrating or swapping instruments.

performance.title: GxP Compliance and LabX Connectivity Explained
performance.description: What a regulated lab actually needs from a balance, and where MX204 delivers it.
body: A weighing result in a GxP-regulated environment has to survive an audit, not just be accurate in the moment. That means the data trail matters as much as the number on the display: who weighed it, when, on what instrument, and whether the record can be tampered with after the fact. A balance that isn't built for that leaves the audit trail to manual logbooks and printouts, both easy to lose and easy to challenge.

MX204 is built GxP-compliant from the ground up, and connects directly to Mettler Toledo's LabX software, so weighing results move into a controlled, traceable record automatically rather than depending on someone transcribing a number correctly.

performance.title: IP43 and Passcode Protection Explained
performance.description: What durability and access control actually add in a lab that isn't a clean, controlled analytical bench.
body: A precision balance handling larger, everyday samples usually lives in a busier corner of the lab than an analytical balance: more dust in the air, more chance of a splash, more hands using it across a shift. Neither of those risks stops accurate weighing on their own, but together they wear down an instrument that isn't built for the environment, and they open the door to settings being changed by whoever's standing there.

MA1002's IP43 rating protects against dust ingress and splashing water, and passcode protection restricts who can access or change balance settings, so the instrument holds up physically and the configuration stays under control, regardless of how busy or shared the bench gets.

body: A precision balance handling larger, heavier samples faces two everyday risks a lighter analytical balance rarely sees: the instrument itself shifting or tipping under an off-center load, and a sample or vessel accidentally set down too hard or too heavy for the pan. performance.description: What automation actually removes from a routine that repeats trace-level weighing many times a day.
body: Trace-level weighing at 1 µg readability is precise enough on a single measurement, but a routine that repeats the same weighing steps dozens of times a day introduces its own risk: a skipped step, an inconsistent sequence, or a small variation in how each sample is handled compounds across a batch.
